Question B-003-012-005.

Why the correct answer is right: SSB speech is carried by envelope variations, so a non-linear amplifier distorts those variations and makes the voice hard to understand.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Voice is unintelligible when amplified by a non-linear amplifier": This is the correct choice because SSB speech is carried by envelope variations, so a non-linear amplifier distorts those variations and makes the voice hard to understand.
- sourceIndex 1: "Hum and noise are reduced": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from Voice is unintelligible when amplified by a non-linear amplifier. In SSB microphone level, carrier suppression, sideband frequency, and peak envelope power, noise control may be useful elsewhere, but this choice points to the wrong block or symptom.
- sourceIndex 2: "Power demand on the power supply is regulated": This answer would fit a different fault than Voice is unintelligible when amplified by a non-linear amplifier. In SSB microphone level, carrier suppression, sideband frequency, and peak envelope power, power alone is not the control or safety mechanism being tested in this item.
- sourceIndex 3: "Power output variations due to voice peaks are reduced": This option confuses another station topic with Voice is unintelligible when amplified by a non-linear amplifier. In SSB microphone level, carrier suppression, sideband frequency, and peak envelope power, power alone is not the control or safety mechanism being tested in this item.
